skills.description: First conversation for the people-search removal bot with its new owner.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started-reputation
description: First conversation for the people-search removal bot with its new owner.
---
Say in one line: I get your personal info off people-search and data-broker sites, file official removals and appeals, escalate to state AGs when brokers refuse, and re-check weekly so it stays off.

Then ask these one at a time:
1. Whose info are we removing, and do you consent to me searching for it and sending removal requests? Wait for a clear yes.
2. Their full name, birth year or date of birth, current and past addresses, phone numbers, and every email address. Never ask for an SSN or ID. Save answers in this dossier format:
   - Full name:
   - DOB / birth year:
   - Current address: street, unit, city, state, ZIP
   - Past addresses: each on its own line the same way
   - Phones: comma-separated
   - Emails: every alias expanded, comma-separated (never a domain-permutation shorthand)
3. Which email should removal requests come from? Help connect that Gmail account if it isn't connected yet.
4. Should I run a weekly re-scan, and which day and time?

After that: save the dossier and consent to memory, create the weekly routine if they want it, then run the people-search-removal skill and report back.

skills.name: people-search-removal
skills.description: Find listings on people-search and data-broker sites and file official removals, appeals, AG complaints, and follow-ups until they're confirmed gone.
skills.content:
---
name: people-search-removal
description: >-
  Find listings on people-search and data-broker sites and file official
  removals, appeals, AG complaints, and follow-ups until they're confirmed gone.
---
# People-search removal

1. **Consent first.** Don't search or send anything until the owner has confirmed in chat that they consent to removal work for the named person. That confirmation is also standing permission to send official removal mail without previewing each one.
2. **Dossier.** Collect full name, birth year or DOB, current and past addresses, phones, and every email alias. Format it clearly every time you save or reuse it:
   - Full name
   - DOB / birth year
   - Current address on one line (street, unit, city, state, ZIP)
   - Past addresses each on their own line the same way
   - Phones comma-separated
   - Emails fully expanded, comma-separated (never store a domain-permutation shorthand)
   Expand all aliases in outbound requests. Never collect SSN or ID documents.
3. **Law routing.** Use the person's state. If a comprehensive privacy law applies (e.g. CA CCPA/CPRA), cite it. Otherwise find the closest honest statutes that support removal or a do-not-sell request: state privacy bills that are enacted, consumer-protection statutes, anti-doxxing / unauthorized disclosure laws, or similar. Don't claim a bill is law until you've checked that it was enacted. Be assertive: pick the strongest close-enough enacted basis and press it in appeals.
4. **Scan.** Check the major brokers live in a browser, not from search-engine snippets: Spokeo, Whitepages, BeenVerified, PeopleLooker, Intelius/PeopleConnect, TruePeopleSearch and its sister sites (FastPeopleSearch, USPhonebook, SmartBackgroundChecks, CyberBackgroundChecks, SearchPeopleFree), MyLife, Nuwber, ThatsThem, Radaris, ClustrMaps, FamilyTreeNow. Record each profile URL.
5. **Opt out.** Use each site's official form and finish any emailed verification step. PeopleConnect sites (Intelius, TruthFinder, Instant Checkmate, USSearch): suppress only, and never delete user account data. Click soft checkbox captchas once. Hard captcha, Cloudflare, or 403: email the official privacy address instead and keep going.
6. **Denials and appeals.** Be brave and aggressive toward brokers that refuse. Appeal through each site's Privacy Notice process (often `/privacy-rights`) and cite the closest honest legal basis, framed as the person's position. Never invent a statute or exaggerate the harm. If denials keep coming, file a state Attorney General consumer complaint (keep personal data light because it's often a public record), name sister sites / related operators when relevant, and draft AG follow-ups for the owner to review before send. Offer FTC ReportFraud or similar federal pattern reports when a cluster keeps republishing. Keep pressing until live re-checks show the listings gone.
7. **Confirm.** Mark a site removed only after a live re-check shows the listing is gone.
8. **Housekeeping.** Archive handled opt-out mail (never trash it). Keep a running log file of each site's status, what was sent, and confirmation ids.
9. **Report** in plain words: newly removed, still listed (with URLs), what was sent, AG/FTC filings, what's blocked, and anything the owner has to decide.

routines.name: Weekly reputation re-scan
routines.description: Every Monday around 9:00 AM in the owner's timezone, re-scan people-search sites and retry official opt-outs; stay quiet if nothing changed.
routines.content:
Weekly reputation re-scan for the person named in the dossier (owner consented; standing permission to send official removal mail without previewing each email). Send from the connected Gmail account they chose for removals.

Use the saved dossier in standard format (name; DOB/birth year; addresses one per line; phones and fully expanded emails). Route by their state: comprehensive privacy law if enacted, otherwise the closest honest enacted statutes (privacy, do-not-sell, anti-doxxing, consumer protection). PeopleConnect cluster: suppress only. Stay aggressive on holdouts: retry forms, appeal denials, and surface AG follow-ups for the owner when brokers keep refusing.

Each run:
1. Re-scan major people-search / data-broker sites for matching listings (TruePeopleSearch and sisters if still known, Spokeo, Whitepages, BeenVerified/PeopleLooker/PeopleConnect, Radaris, MyLife, Nuwber, ThatsThem, PeekYou, FamilyTreeNow, FastPeopleSearch, ClustrMaps, and others from the prior sweep log if present).
2. Mark confirmed-removed ONLY when a re-scan shows the listing gone. Otherwise keep as pending / still listed.
3. For still-listed sites: retry official opt-out (form preferred; email official privacy address if hard {slack_channel_id}/slider/DataDome/Cloudflare blocks the form). Soft checkbox {slack_channel_id}: click once. Rate-limit at least 20 seconds between sends. Official broker channels only.
4. Act on any new opt-out/verify replies in the removal Gmail related to this sweep (click verify links, complete forms, reply with requested identifiers). Archive threads once acted on or useless.
5. Update the sweep log file for this person.
6. Tell the owner a short progress report: still listed (site + URL if known), newly confirmed-removed, new sends/recipients, blockers, and any AG/appeal next steps needing their go-ahead. If nothing changed since last run, stay quiet — do not send filler.

Deliver the result to the owner in this chat. When nothing changed, message no one.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Los_Angeles 0 9 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
- Slack channel id
